sources_checked.finding: Creating interface costs energy; contraction favors less area subject to constraints. Force is along the moved boundary, consistent with tangential film pulls.

claim_checks.finding: The small isolated free bubble, positive surface energy, and least-area sphere for prescribed enclosed volume are supported. A fixed idealized volume is explicitly stated, avoiding the claim that all real detaching bubbles preserve exact volume.

The prescribed 3D semiaxis multipliers k, k^(-1/2), k^(-1/2) have product 1, preserving ellipsoid volume. This is an independent mathematical check of the storyboard, not a check of renderer implementation.
English small/free/tends and Traditional Chinese 小/自由漂浮/漸漸接近 preserve the stated context. Final same-space line is tied to the idealized comparison, not an unqualified measured bubble law.

production_conditions: Keep the equal-volume comparison three-dimensional; preserving only 2D silhouette area would fail the stated model.
Render surface-tension pulls tangent to a film patch, not independent inward radial force arrows.
Label fixed-volume morph and timing as schematic; retain isolated small free bubble and do not generalize to frames or foam.
limitations: Desk/source review only; no physical experiment or complete source videos watched.

sources_checked.finding: Needle is a freely pivoting magnet, aligning with the local field; local interference can affect its direction.

sources_checked.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources_checked.locator: Compass FAQ, extracted lines 120–143; field components around lines 28–37
sources_checked.finding: Compass aligns with the horizontal component at its location, not one exact point. Declination distinguishes magnetic bearing from true north. Horizontal field can be too weak near magnetic poles.

claim_checks.finding: The level pivoting magnetic needle aligns with the horizontal local field; the ordinary stable-field scene can retain needle direction as housing turns. True north and magnetic heading are correctly separated.

English 'part of that field runs along the ground' and Chinese 水平方向 agree with the horizontal-component model. The marked end is the north-seeking end and the illustrated true/magnetic angle is qualitative.

production_conditions: Hold overhead camera, map and local field fixed while only the case rotates in hook/return; separately perturb the needle for alignment.
Identify the north-seeking marked end, and never imply the needle points to a single exact geographic or magnetic pole.
Use a level ordinary compass in a nonzero horizontal field away from magnetic-pole blackout regions and interfering magnets/metal; exaggerated declination is a schematic angle.
limitations: Page/transcript text was read; the audio was not listened to in full.
At magnetic poles or strong local interference the ordinary direction scene fails; this is excluded by the production condition.
No rendered needle/case motion or source-specific present-day declination verified. Exact script PASS is not visual/encode approval.
